page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 12 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 12 physical cores with 1 thread per core and a cache hierarchy including 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. It includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 10.67 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, falls within the average middle 50% tier, reflecting the shared CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as read-only large block at 146.11 GB/sec and write large block at 89.37 GB/sec, also place in the average tier. For AI workloads, LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model achieves a top-tier rate of 349.81 tokens/sec, while prompt processing for the same model operates at an average rate of 1842.33 tokens/sec.

The server presents a specific resource density tradeoff, pairing high-end dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs and a large 128 GB memory footprint with shared CPU allocation and a lack of local storage. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require heavy GPU acceleration and substantial system memory but do not demand dedicated, constant CPU cores or local storage. Appropriate workloads include GPU-accelerated machine learning inference, data science tasks, and parallel processing jobs that leverage the Ada Lovelace architecture and AVX-512 instruction sets.
